ruling: R32 (Drew, 2026-09-14, "SPLIT MOVES") + R55 (Drew, 2026-09-15, "the title may not name more than the destination"): a split-identity row (cardId != hobbyiqCardId) moves to the checklist-backed side ONLY when the title names that side's differing segment(s) on the axis (or axis combination) the row was actually judged on -- setKey, cardNumber, parallel, sport, printRun. reportOnlyUntil: REPORT ONLY until a steward dispatches it. The lane writes only under BACKFILL_APPLY=true. parseApplyScope permanently refuses "split"/"r32" from writing -- this list is the vehicle Drew's ruling names for actually moving the rows the wave judged move-worthy.
provenanceCorrection: TRANCHE 1 CORRECTED PROVENANCE (2026-09-16). The first cut of this list was built from the WRONG wave -- 18 census-slot-N.json artifacts pulled from run ids 35037777892..35037932269 (head f75ea51f56a207e59c3d53f0c0157b9447ee66fb, dispatched 2026-09-15 ~23:53-23:57Z), which is a LATER, separate apply-improve wave (concurrent with/after the R33 dispatch), not the R32 wave the coordinator's brief actually named. The GENUINE R32 wave is run ids 34989338372..34989448708 (head a87b59fca683b441e912b491edec03517ee5647d, dispatched 2026-09-15 ~15:34:17-15:35:17Z), all 32 of which are now terminal (status=completed, conclusion=success) and all 32 of whose census-slot-N.json artifacts are pulled here. Confirmed the two heads carry BYTE-IDENTICAL backend/scripts/lib/split-scope.cjs (`git diff a87b59fc f75ea51f -- backend/scripts/lib/split-scope.cjs` produces no output) -- the R55 split-move/park JUDGMENT LOGIC was never in question, only which run's artifacts this list's row samples came from. This corrected build reproduces the wave's own reported totals EXACTLY: splitIdentity.scopes.split.move summed across all 32 slots = 17,313; .park summed = 1,090,004; total judged = 1,107,317 -- matching the coordinator's brief to the row.
finding: This list is built from the R32 wave's own moveSamples arrays (splitIdentity.scopes.split.byAxis.<axis>.moveSamples in each slot's census-slot-N.json artifact), NOT from the console-log capture the steward saved to $S/r32-wave-would-move-2026-09-16.md + .jsonl -- those files carry the generic split-identity SAMPLE lines (id/class/cardId||hobbyiqCardId/differing-segments) for ALL derivation classes, not the R32-specific move verdict, and the console log never prints moveSamples/parkSamples at all (only the aggregate per-axis move/park counts).
coverageNote: All 32 of 32 dispatched slots' census-slot-N.json artifacts were recovered and included (see provenanceTable below for the exact run id per slot -- all head a87b59fca683b441e912b491edec03517ee5647d). Even with full 32/32 slot coverage, THIS LIST CANNOT REACH THE FULL 17,313 WOULD-MOVE POPULATION, structurally: each slot's census caps moveSamples at 50 rows PER AXIS (SPLIT_SCOPE_SAMPLE_CAP in rematch-sold-comps.cjs), and the setKey axis alone carries 17,262 of the 17,313 real move rows -- 32 slots x 50 samples = a 1,600-row ceiling for setKey, regardless of how many slots are included. Appending more slots cannot close this gap because there are no more slots to append (32/32 is already everything); the cap itself is the limit. This list holds 1,894 distinct rows -- everything the current census artifact shape can ever produce for this wave. The coordinator is commissioning an EXPORT MODE in split-scope.cjs (uncapped or differently-capped) to reach the full 17,313; this PR is TRANCHE 1 under that plan, built from what the existing capped artifacts already carry, not a partial pull awaiting more slots.
refusalRule: A row refuses (is excluded from this list) when its fromCardId/fromHobbyiqCardId differ on any segment OUTSIDE the row's own judged-axis set. The judged-axis set is read from the row's own `reason` string (title-names-destination:<dest>:<axis1,axis2,...>) -- the authoritative source, since the fleet's per-axis moveSamples arrays are independently capped at 50 each and a row's SAMPLE can land in fewer axis buckets than it was actually judged on. auto/cardYear/grade differences are never in scope for R32 and are excluded from the refusal check. 0 of 1,894 candidate rows were refused -- every row's real slug diff, re-measured directly from fromCardId/fromHobbyiqCardId, stayed within its own judged axes.
pointReadVerification: 200-row evenly-spread sample (every ~9th entry) point-read by id+partitionKey=fromCardId against the live sold_comps container: 200/200 still resident at fromCardId, 200/200 with hobbyiqCardId unchanged from the census's own capture (0 moved-away, 0 not-found, 0 hobbyiqCardId-since-changed).
shapeNote: destination="cardId" in the wave's own verdict means the row's OWN cardId (partition) is the checklist-backed side -- shape="repoint" here, no partition change, only hobbyiqCardId is patched to match. destination="hobbyiqCardId" means the row's hobbyiqCardId is checklist-backed -- shape="relocate", the partition (cardId) moves to match hobbyiqCardId, which itself stays unchanged.
